correctness.rationale: Every possible cycle pattern for lengths two and three is exhausted. For length two, \(P(p+k)=p\) is equivalent to the stated factorization condition. For length three, prime/composite alternation forces the pattern prime-prime-composite, then \(p\mid2k\) and primality of \(p+k\) force \(p=2\); the remaining largest-prime-factor condition is exactly \(k+1\) a power of two. Converses are checked explicitly. The finite verifier is supplementary only.
